questions.q: Which principle does the lesson recommend for making a new AI habit stick?
options: Wait until you find a big, perfect use case before you start
Spend at least an hour a day so the habit builds faster
Attach it to a routine you already have, like your morning coffee
Restart the whole plan from Day 1 whenever you miss a day
questions.explain: An existing routine is the best trigger for a new one, as in "After my morning coffee, I'll use AI for one task." Starting small and keeping a simple log also help the habit stick.

questions.q: You're on Day 12 of the plan and a busy week makes you miss three days in a row. What should you do?
options: Start the 30-day plan over from Day 1 so you do it properly
Make up for the missed days by doing all of them at once
Stop the plan, since missed days mean the habit has failed
Pick up where you left off, with a two-minute version if needed
questions.explain: Don't restart the plan; pick up where you left off. Missing a day doesn't break a habit, but quitting does, and on a busy day you can do a two-minute version.

questions.q: A new AI feature is announced and you're worried about falling behind. What does the lesson suggest?
options: Ask your assistant to explain it, then try it on one real task
Switch to whichever assistant launched the newest feature
Follow every announcement closely so you never miss a change
Ignore it, since new features never matter for everyday use
questions.explain: You don't need to chase every announcement, because context, iteration, verification and privacy work with any assistant. When a new feature appears, ask your assistant to explain it, then try it on one real task.
